claims.head: Pettersson (#40) gets company tonight
claims.call: The Islanders’ L4 (Pageau, Duclair and Holmström) spends at least 43% of its 5-on-5 time against the Canucks’ second line.
claims.body: At home, the Islanders keep sending Holmström’s line (Pageau, Duclair and Holmström) out against opponents’ second lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Peter DeBoer has been using this group as a checking line on opponents’ second lines. Tonight the Canucks’ second line is DeBrusk, Pettersson (#40) and Lekkerimäki.

notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 7 games cover only 25% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the second-lowest in the league (a typical team: 47%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
M. Sasson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 32% of the team’s shorthanded time in 7 games, up from 4% last season.
A. Bains has started killing penalties: on the ice for 26% of the team’s shorthanded time in 6 games, up from 3% last season.
M. Barzal is on the injured non-roster list (knee injury) and has not played this season. He is one of their most valuable skaters. V. Eklund has taken his spot beside B. Schenn and C. Ritchie.
K. Palmieri is no longer killing penalties: 0% of the team’s shorthanded time in 5 games, down from 37% last season.

NYI.head: The Islanders should be favored
NYI.body: Even though the Islanders will be without Barzal, the Islanders have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. Vancouver’s best way in is getting good looks.

VAN.head: Vancouver has their work cut out
VAN.body: Even though the Islanders will be without Barzal, the Islanders have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. Vancouver’s best hope is getting good looks, plus a big night in goal.

story.head: The Canucks need a win
paras: The Islanders are 2-3-0. The Canucks are on a four-game losing streak.
